evidence: Judged: DRAFT "When you're done, make sure to come back the other way." CONTEXT holds it once, in the second paragraph under "Please don’t put six metaphors in one trance", after "If you're going to count, do it in a way that makes sense in your world." and before the parenthetical "(You can borrow qualities, but don't change who you are.)". Change check: SOURCE words are "And when you're done, come back the other way."; the draft drops "And" and adds "make sure to", nothing else, which is what the_change says (Emulate's sentence, no AI fix). Meaning check: SOURCE meaning is the published guide's "reverse the journey when you finish"; "come back the other way" is untouched, and "make sure to" only stresses a step that was already an imperative, so no new claim, fact, first-person content or named entity is added. Reading in context: a first-time reader takes "When you're done" as the end of the trance or count just described, and "the other way" still has the same anchors the source had (the count in the sentence before, and "one way of coming back" in the first paragraph), so it reads as: come out by reversing how you went in. Dropping "And" does not strand it; it becomes the next tip in a list of tips. The only pronoun is "you" (the reader), so there is no referent problem (C02 checked, not present). The straight apostrophe matches the other contractions in that paragraph. "make sure to" also has a job here: the section says metaphors are "entirely optional" and treats the rest as "whatever" or "feel free", so "make sure to" marks the one step that is not optional; I do not read it as filler. It occurs once in this section, and the guide already uses it elsewhere in its own sentences (in another change's context I saw "Make sure you're leaving some time at the end to come back"), so it is in the guide's voice and not a one-off phrase. Tells: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the draft in its paragraph and found none PRESENT. Looked at hardest: T02 (the paragraph is a run of tips, but that cadence is the source's own and this sentence is one step softened by "make sure to", not a compressed verdict; the change does not add to it), T22 (a plain instruction carrying the author's insistence on the return, not reassurance), T07 ("make sure to" is an intensifier doing the job above, not staged hesitation), T15 (no swap to rarer words), T26 ("come back" echoes "one way of coming back" in paragraph one, but that is the source's own and the repetition is the same step), T13 and T09 (the two D9 pointers: the paragraph keeps its asides (the signal list ending in "lack of signal, whatever" and the borrow-qualities parenthetical), the section adds more ("just do one"), and the sentences carry uneven weight, so it is not slot-filling), T20 and T29 (it is not the paragraph's last sentence, and it adds no restatement). Linter findings: (1) "D9 follows the source order": accepted. The change swaps one sentence in its own slot and does not reorder or add a point, and organization alone is not a tell; the paragraph notices things along the way (see T13/T09 above). (2) "E36/E41 heavy second person" (9.1 you per 100 words): accepted. The guide is addressed to the reader throughout, and the draft has one "you're", the same as the sentence it replaces, so it adds no second-person density (it adds two net words) and is not coach register, since it gives an instruction and no reassurance. Side note on the writer's ledger: its T14 and T15 lines say the draft puts back a point Emulate dropped, but this draft is Emulate's own wording with nothing put back, so those two lines are templated; the ABSENT calls are right.
